items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-09
items.q: The interviewee (Nick La Rocca) mentions 'Evelyn Presley' (referred to as 'poor Evelyn Presley' and later 'Elvin Presley' due to transcription error) in the context of a newspaper article criticizing the press for not writing about him. There is no indication of a personal relationship, meeting, or

ctx.x: Robichaud and there wasn't another one. Manuel Perez had a note-reading band. And they played by notes. They played almost the same as white men. They had nothing to it. They played just what was on the paper, like on a score. They say different today. That's not so. Never has been so. And Negroes never has been in the sentence in the music field until only lately. Some time ago they had an article in the item. What they didn't say about poor Evelyn Presley, I couldn't begin to tell you.

Their champion was a colored man. Let's say a colored man has his rightful place in any music. Why not the white man to eulogize another man that hasn't created anything because of his color? That must be his music. But although Elvin Presley went on to hikes while the other guy stayed there, if you listen to his style, he couldn't have been original because he changed four or five different times. First his rhythm was based on the tango. Then he changed it to something else. Elvin Presley stuck to one style and…
